ticket.summary: Customer's garbage disposal hummed without spinning; talked her through safe self-clear and she removed a peach pit — unit fully working, no visit needed.
mitigation_advice: Switch off and unplug the disposal (or trip its breaker) and never reach into the drain by hand
Insert a 1/4" hex/Allen wrench into the hole on the underside center of the unit and rock it back and forth until the impeller spins freely
Remove any visible debris with tongs, restore power, press the red reset button, then run cold water and test
Prevention: keep pits, bones, fibrous scraps and grease out; run cold water before, during and ~20 seconds after grinding
Call back if it hums again after wrenching or repeatedly trips the reset — likely a failing motor needing replacement
ticket.customer_message: Woohoo — a peach pit! Classic disposal killer. Nicely done, you fixed it yourself. Two quick tips so it doesn't happen again: keep pits, bones, fibrous stuff (celery, corn husks) and grease out, and always run cold water before, during, and ~20 seconds after grinding. If it ever hums again and the wrench doesn't free it, or it trips the reset repeatedly, that usually means the motor's going — give us a call and we'll take a look. No charge tonight, and we'll be back at the phones tomorrow at 8am. Take care!
